job_description: ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE CHIEF RISK OFFICER Appointment of the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) Appointment of the CRO would be for a fixed tenure of 3 years from the date of appointment, with the approval of the Board of Directors. Further, any extension in the tenure will also be approved by the Board.The CRO may be transferred / removed from his post during his tenure or on / after expiry of his tenure only with the approval of the Board.Transfer / removal of the CRO shall be reported to the Department of Banking Supervision, Reserve Bank of India, Mumbai. Any change in incumbency of CRO shall also be reported to the stock exchanges. Reporting structure The CRO shall have direct reporting line to the Managing Director & CEO of the Bank. The RMC/ the Chairperson of the RMC/ person nominated by the Chairperson of the RMC shall meet the CRO on one-to-one basis, without the presence of the Managing Director & CEO, at least on a quarterly basis.He / she shall not have any reporting relationship with the business verticals of the bank and shall not be given any business targets.He / she shall not be given the responsibility of Chief Executive Officer, Chief Operating Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Audit Executive or any other function. Qualifications The CRO should have the organizational stature, authority and the necessary skills to oversee the Bank's risk management activities. He / she should be independent and have duties distinct from other executive functions. He / she should have had adequate experience in banking/ financial services across business, operations and/ or control functions.CA / MBA / FRM or other such qualification required to be a member of the Risk Department as per any Board approved policy in this respect Experience More than 20 years of experience in multiple roles (e.g. business, governance, risk etc.)More than 10 years of experience in roles in control functions.Experience in Banking space in a leadership role he CRO should have the organizational stature, authority and the necessary skills to oversee Scope CRO shall have oversight over the Bank as well as the subsidiaries of the Bank. Roles & Responsibilities of the CRO Primary responsibility for risk management function He / she has the primary responsibility for overseeing the development and implementation of the Bank's risk management function.CRO shall be the Head of the Risk Department. He / she is responsible for the costs, facilities and manpower in the Department.He / she is also responsible for ensuring that the employees of the Department comply with the rules and regulations of the Bank.CRO can delegate the responsibilities herein to the officials in the Risk Department as may be appropriate. Responsibilities around frameworks and governanceHe / she is responsible for supporting the Board in defining the Bank's risk appetite statement (RAS) and its implementation by cascading it across the Bank. He / she, together with the management, should be actively engaged in the process of setting risk measures and limits for the various business lines and monitoring their performance in alignment with RAS.He / she is responsible for putting in place policies and procedures designed to manage the risk profile of the Bank, and for ensuring appropriate governance thereof through people and systems wherever needed. He / she is also responsible for the models, data, systems and reporting frameworks that are required for suitable risk management. Operational responsibilities His / her responsibilities also include participating in key decision-making processes that impact the risk profile of the Bank (e.g. strategic, capital and liquidity planning, new products and services).He / she shall represent the Risk Department at various senior management committees including committees of the Board where applicable, on risk issues emanating from frauds, IT, business strategy, operations, retail & corporate credit, investments and trading, and overseas business. CRO is responsible for managing the interaction with audit, accounting and compliance functions and regulators, including risk based submissions to regulators.He / she should communicate, effectively and in a timely manner the risks that impact the Bank, both across the organization and through reporting to the board and senior management. He / she must help build an appropriate Risk Culture within the organization. Role of CRO in Credit Sanctioning Process For 'large' credit proposals ('large' is being defined as above Rs. 750 Cr. In borrower exposure, covering Mid Corporate, Large Corporate, Financial Institutions, NBFC/HFC, Capital Markets Division, Government Banking, New Economy Group and Stressed Assets Group segments)The role of CRO will be that of an Adviser.CRO will be a permanent invitee at the meetings of Senior Management Committee (SMC) and Committee of Directors (COD), where proposals of the above referred segments are put up for sanction.CRO will provide his views on each of these large credit proposals.CRO will not have any voting rights in the meetings of the above committees.For proposals pertaining to the above segments and which are not 'large' or are not being referred to SMC/COD, the Risk Department, apart from confirming the Internal Rating, will be recording its views on matters pertaining to exposure / portfolio as governed by the RAS and Guardrails approved by Risk Management Committee. Why This Role Matters
1) Protects the Bank’s P&L and Capital
Maximizes recoveries from the NPA pool and minimizes fresh slippages, directly impacting credit costs, provisions, and write-offs.
Controls delinquency and forward flow to keep Stage 2/Stage 3 exposures in check, improving ECL (Expected Credit Loss) outcomes and preserving profitability.
2) Safeguards Asset Quality & Enterprise Risk
By meeting monthly resolution targets and arresting bucket movement, the role ensures a stable GNPA/NNPA trajectory.
A strong contingency plan protects collections continuity during disruptions (macro shocks, local events, tech outages), reducing operational and reputational risk.

Agency governance and strict adherence to RBI guidelines and bank’s collection policy prevent misconduct, customer complaints, and supervisory penalties.

5) Drives Operational Excellence at Scale
Manpower planning across assigned locations and agencies ensures adequate capacity for peaks, seasonality, and special drives.
Performance-oriented culture (clear KPIs, reviews, coaching) converts targets into predictable outcomes and higher productivity.
6) Builds Capability & Process Maturity
Training on products, processes, and policies creates a skilled team equipped to handle complex accounts, restructuring norms, and digital tools.
Strong MIS and early warning (DPD buckets, roll rates, broken promises, geography trends) supports proactive interventions.

Works closely with Sales, Credit, Legal, Risk, Ops, and Digital to enable normalization, settlements, restructuring, legal actions, and process fixes—driving end-to-end asset health.

role_summary:
1) Protects the Bank’s P&L and Capital
Maximizes recoveries from the NPA pool and minimizes fresh slippages, directly impacting credit costs, provisions, and write-offs.
Controls delinquency and forward flow to keep Stage 2/Stage 3 exposures in check, improving ECL (Expected Credit Loss) outcomes and preserving profitability.
2) Safeguards Asset Quality & Enterprise Risk
By meeting monthly resolution targets and arresting bucket movement, the role ensures a stable GNPA/NNPA trajectory.
A strong contingency plan protects collections continuity during disruptions (macro shocks, local events, tech outages), reducing operational and reputational risk.

Agency governance and strict adherence to RBI guidelines and bank’s collection policy prevent misconduct, customer complaints, and supervisory penalties.
Process and audit discipline (call logs, dunning, field visits, consent, privacy, grievance) ensures audit readiness and policy conformance.
4) Elevates Customer Experience While Recovering Dues
Professional, compliant collections practices build trust, reduce complaints, and enable win-back/normalization—supporting future cross-sell and retention.
5) Drives Operational Excellence at Scale
Manpower planning across assigned locations and agencies ensures adequate capacity for peaks, seasonality, and special drives.
Performance-oriented culture (clear KPIs, reviews, coaching) converts targets into predictable outcomes and higher productivity.
6) Builds Capability & Process Maturity
Training on products, processes, and policies creates a skilled team equipped to handle complex accounts, restructuring norms, and digital tools.
Strong MIS and early warning (DPD buckets, roll rates, broken promises, geography trends) supports proactive interventions.
7) Strengthens Cross-Functional Delivery
Works closely with Sales, Credit, Legal, Risk, Ops, and Digital to enable normalization, settlements, restructuring, legal actions, and process fixes—driving end-to-end asset health.

Works closely with Sales, Credit, Legal, Risk, Ops, and Digital to enable normalization, settlements, restructuring, legal actions, and process fixes—driving end-to-end asset health.

role_summary:
1) Protects the Bank’s P&L and Capital
Maximizes recoveries from the NPA pool and minimizes fresh slippages, directly impacting credit costs, provisions, and write-offs.
Controls delinquency and forward flow to keep Stage 2/Stage 3 exposures in check, improving ECL (Expected Credit Loss) outcomes and preserving profitability.
2) Safeguards Asset Quality & Enterprise Risk
By meeting monthly resolution targets and arresting bucket movement, the role ensures a stable GNPA/NNPA trajectory.
A strong contingency plan protects collections continuity during disruptions (macro shocks, local events, tech outages), reducing operational and reputational risk.
3) Ensures Regulatory & Policy Compliance (RBI + Bank)
Agency governance and strict adherence to RBI guidelines and bank’s collection policy prevent misconduct, customer complaints, and supervisory penalties.
Process and audit discipline (call logs, dunning, field visits, consent, privacy, grievance) ensures audit readiness and policy conformance.
4) Elevates Customer Experience While Recovering Dues
Professional, compliant collections practices build trust, reduce complaints, and enable win-back/normalization—supporting future cross-sell and retention.
5) Drives Operational Excellence at Scale
Manpower planning across assigned locations and agencies ensures adequate capacity for peaks, seasonality, and special drives.
Performance-oriented culture (clear KPIs, reviews, coaching) converts targets into predictable outcomes and higher productivity.
6) Builds Capability & Process Maturity
Training on products, processes, and policies creates a skilled team equipped to handle complex accounts, restructuring norms, and digital tools.
Strong MIS and early warning (DPD buckets, roll rates, broken promises, geography trends) supports proactive interventions.
7) Strengthens Cross-Functional Delivery
Works closely with Sales, Credit, Legal, Risk, Ops, and Digital to enable normalization, settlements, restructuring, legal actions, and process fixes—driving end-to-end asset health.

Maximizes recoveries from the NPA pool and minimizes fresh slippages, directly impacting credit costs, provisions, and write-offs.
Controls delinquency and forward flow to keep Stage 2/Stage 3 exposures in check, improving ECL (Expected Credit Loss) outcomes and preserving profitability.

Professional, compliant collections practices build trust, reduce complaints, and enable win-back/normalization—supporting future cross-sell and retention.

Performance-oriented culture (clear KPIs, reviews, coaching) converts targets into predictable outcomes and higher productivity.

Works closely with Sales, Credit, Legal, Risk, Ops, and Digital to enable normalization, settlements, restructuring, legal actions, and process fixes—driving end-to-end asset health.

Maximizes recoveries from the NPA pool and minimizes fresh slippages, directly impacting credit costs, provisions, and write-offs.
Controls delinquency and forward flow to keep Stage 2/Stage 3 exposures in check, improving ECL (Expected Credit Loss) outcomes and preserving profitability.

Professional, compliant collections practices build trust, reduce complaints, and enable win-back/normalization—supporting future cross-sell and retention.

Manpower planning across assigned locations and agencies ensures adequate capacity for peaks, seasonality, and special drives.
Performance-oriented culture (clear KPIs, reviews, coaching) converts targets into predictable outcomes and higher productivity.
6) Builds Capability & Process Maturity
Training on products, processes, and policies creates a skilled team equipped to handle complex accounts, restructuring norms, and digital tools.
Strong MIS and early warning (DPD buckets, roll rates, broken promises, geography trends) supports proactive interventions.
7) Strengthens Cross-Functional Delivery
Works closely with Sales, Credit, Legal, Risk, Ops, and Digital to enable normalization, settlements, restructuring, legal actions, and process fixes—driving end-to-end asset health.

Performance-oriented culture (clear KPIs, reviews, coaching) converts targets into predictable outcomes and higher productivity.

Professional, compliant collections practices build trust, reduce complaints, and enable win-back/normalization—supporting future cross-sell and retention.

Performance-oriented culture (clear KPIs, reviews, coaching) converts targets into predictable outcomes and higher productivity.

Training on products, processes, and policies creates a skilled team equipped to handle complex accounts, restructuring norms, and digital tools.
Strong MIS and early warning (DPD buckets, roll rates, broken promises, geography trends) supports proactive interventions.

Works closely with Sales, Credit, Legal, Risk, Ops, and Digital to enable normalization, settlements, restructuring, legal actions, and process fixes—driving end-to-end asset health.

role_summary:
1) Protects the Bank’s P&L and Capital
Maximizes recoveries from the NPA pool and minimizes fresh slippages, directly impacting credit costs, provisions, and write-offs.
Controls delinquency and forward flow to keep Stage 2/Stage 3 exposures in check, improving ECL (Expected Credit Loss) outcomes and preserving profitability.
2) Safeguards Asset Quality & Enterprise Risk
By meeting monthly resolution targets and arresting bucket movement, the role ensures a stable GNPA/NNPA trajectory.
A strong contingency plan protects collections continuity during disruptions (macro shocks, local events, tech outages), reducing operational and reputational risk.
3) Ensures Regulatory & Policy Compliance (RBI + Bank)
Agency governance and strict adherence to RBI guidelines and bank’s collection policy prevent misconduct, customer complaints, and supervisory penalties.
Process and audit discipline (call logs, dunning, field visits, consent, privacy, grievance) ensures audit readiness and policy conformance.
4) Elevates Customer Experience While Recovering Dues
Professional, compliant collections practices build trust, reduce complaints, and enable win-back/normalization—supporting future cross-sell and retention.
5) Drives Operational Excellence at Scale
Manpower planning across assigned locations and agencies ensures adequate capacity for peaks, seasonality, and special drives.
Performance-oriented culture (clear KPIs, reviews, coaching) converts targets into predictable outcomes and higher productivity.
6) Builds Capability & Process Maturity
Training on products, processes, and policies creates a skilled team equipped to handle complex accounts, restructuring norms, and digital tools.
Strong MIS and early warning (DPD buckets, roll rates, broken promises, geography trends) supports proactive interventions.
7) Strengthens Cross-Functional Delivery
Works closely with Sales, Credit, Legal, Risk, Ops, and Digital to enable normalization, settlements, restructuring, legal actions, and process fixes—driving end-to-end asset health.

Controls delinquency and forward flow to keep Stage 2/Stage 3 exposures in check, improving ECL (Expected Credit Loss) outcomes and preserving profitability.

Performance-oriented culture (clear KPIs, reviews, coaching) converts targets into predictable outcomes and higher productivity.
